headline: High risk of data leakage and cascading errors: transformers can read/write and browse by default while LightZero is non-runnable and non-I/O, making the pair unsafe for shared-workflow use.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightZero has no filesystem, browser, MCP, or subprocess surfaces, so it cannot directly ingest transformers output by default. transformers can read files and use stdin/stdout, so a manual or file-based bridge could carry prompt-injection content, but the pathway is unusual and the blast radius is limited to the bridged content.
conditions: IF an operator copies transformers output into a file or stdin that LightZero later consumes
IF a shared workspace is introduced between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable manual copy-paste between outputs and prompts
Review any file passed from transformers before reuse
Use a provenance tag on bridged artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: transformers can read the filesystem, browse, and call external APIs, so any shared workspace can expose file contents to its inference backend or third parties. LightZero touches no data classes and has no I/O, so it is not the leak source, but it can still be the origin of files that transformers reads and transmits.
conditions: IF both agents share a directory containing sensitive files
IF transformers is pointed at files produced by LightZero
mitigations: Store each agent in a separate directory
Do not mount sensitive folders into transformers

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero cannot write files, modify git, or use subprocesses, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. transformers can write files and spawn subprocesses, but without overlapping write surfaces there is no meaningful conflict between the pair beyond ordinary read-only coexistence.
conditions: IF LightZero is wrapped in an external orchestrator that adds write access
IF both agents are granted write access to the same directory by the host

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightZero is a game-playing system and transformers is a document-processing system with stdin/stdout and API calls, so a pipeline could treat LightZero output as authoritative input for downstream text generation or actions. No verification step is documented, and uncertainty about the exact orchestration should be resolved upward to medium.
conditions: IF transformers consumes LightZero output without an explicit validation step
IF downstream automation acts on transformers' generated text
mitigations: Require schema validation on LightZero outputs
Block automatic action-taking from generated text

E_compliance.rationale: No sensitive data classes, residency constraints, or retention policies are documented for LightZero, while transformers is a general-purpose open-source library with broad data handling. The pairwise compliance risk is therefore limited to undocumented deployment choices rather than an inherent mismatch, and only transformers is relevant here.
conditions: IF the deployment routes regulated data through transformers
IF the operator applies conflicting retention or residency settings outside the documented profiles
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in this pair
